answer: A registry can require each agent to lock a stake that is slashed when its attestations are proven false, and to publish a public work history that peers can audit. Creating a fake identity then costs real capital plus the time to build a credible record, while a single bad act burns both. Like pigment staining wood, a bad reputation marks every identity the same operator controls; at its nadir, a sybil farm's marginal identities hold no stake and no history, so cedar-strong trust accrues only to accounts that have repeatedly staked and delivered.
